extracted.intended_audience: mid-career women PIs in the physical sciences preparing NSF/DOE grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical grant-writing guidance for (particularly female) mid-career principal investigators preparing NSF (and similar) proposals, emphasizing proposal structure, Broader Impacts, reviewer behavior, resubmission, and voice/style. Focused on tactics to make proposals clear, persuasive, and reviewable by heterogeneous panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-document confident claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may unconsciously discount confident claims from women PIs; therefore claims should be heavily supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy: over-document with citations and preliminary data to back up confident statements; provide evidence rather than relying on tone alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use first-person plural
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'we' even for single-PI grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using first-person plural frames the project as a team effort and can help convey scope and shared responsibility; this is recommended even when the PI is the sole lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hedging language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use unnecessary hedges that undercut claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hedging can be interpreted negatively by reviewers; state aims and expected outcomes clearly while acknowledging limitations elsewhere in a Discussion-style framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance language for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts get equal weight in language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the BI section with the same care and specificity as Intellectual Merit; avoid treating BI as an afterthought or boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Broader Impacts specific and outcome-oriented
rubrics_metrics.description: "I will mentor underrepresented students" is too vague — BI activities must be tied to specific outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the specific program, indicate numbers, timelines, measurable outcomes, and how success will be evaluated; show concrete activities and direct links to outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the BI section as substantive and growing
rubrics_metrics.description: The BI section has become longer and more substantive over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate reviewer expectations for detailed BI plans and provide evidence of feasibility and integration with the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of the Project Description
rubrics_metrics.description: 15 pages is short — every paragraph must justify itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise: eliminate fluff, ensure each paragraph advances a key point, use figures to convey complexity quickly, and employ white space for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open with the big-picture question
rubrics_metrics.description: Start the Project Description by stating the overarching scientific question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This orients reviewers immediately; tie the opening to the field-level importance and NSF strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect proposal to NSF strategic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly connect the project to NSF's strategic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that demonstrates relevance to NSF goals where appropriate; reviewers note alignment with funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show fit into the broader field
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how your work fits into the field, not just your lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain field-level impact, connections to other work, and how the project moves the field forward beyond incremental lab-specific advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for a heterogeneous panel and non-experts
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF panels are heterogeneous in expertise; proposals must be clear to non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive jargon, include accessible explanations and schematic figures, and ensure key claims are understandable to reviewers outside your narrow subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the proposal accessible to ad-hoc outside reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'ad hoc' outside reviewer can sink or save you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that central claims, motivation, and significance are clear without deep subfield knowledge; provide enough background and clarity for single-reviewer evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the influence of mail reviewers' written critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Mail reviewers' written critiques carry weight in close cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and address likely critique points in the proposal text itself, since written reviews can tip borderline funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated research-and-education plan for CAREER awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The integrated research-and-education plan must actually integrate for NSF CAREER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design education activities that are clearly woven into the research program (not appended), using existing campus programs and partnerships when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education plan must not be an afterthought
rubrics_metrics.description: Education plan can't be an afterthought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate substantive space to BI/education efforts, show concrete implementation, evaluation methods, and institutional support rather than superficial add-ons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing programs and infrastructure for education/BI
rubrics_metrics.description: Use existing university programs, partnerships, outreach infrastructure rather than inventing ad-hoc activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveraging established programs increases credibility and feasibility; reviewers 'smell' ad-hoc educational add-ons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support must be specific and substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters must be specific and substantive; generic 'I support this project' letters are worse than no letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request letters that describe concrete commitments, roles, and how the letter-writer will contribute or why the support matters; avoid templated or perfunctory letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish co-PI vs. collaborator roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-PI vs. collaborator distinction matters for budget and responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label roles and justify budget allocations; if someone is listed as a co-PI justify their level of effort and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify international collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: International collaborators need extra justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the international contribution is essential, how logistics will be handled, and any added value that couldn't be obtained domestically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission: persistence and addressing panel comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Most NSF grants are funded after multiple submissions; address all panel comments in the project description (not as response document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state substantial revisions in the narrative (e.g., 'we have substantially revised this proposal in response to prior feedback') and incorporate changes into the main text instead of relegating them to an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing revisions in resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame resubmissions as substantially revised based on prior feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise explanatory sentence in the Project Description to orient reviewers to what changed and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start Project Summary last
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the Project Summary after completing the rest of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should reflect the finalized aims, methods, and BI activities; drafting it last ensures accuracy and cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Specific Aims/Project Description first
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the Specific Aims / Project Description before the Project Summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a clear scientific narrative and aims early so that all other sections align with the central plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use staged feedback: internal before external
rubrics_metrics.description: Get internal feedback before external feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish draft internally (colleagues, collaborators, departmental review) to catch technical flaws before seeking broader external reviewers for clarity and general comprehensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read proposals aloud and use non-expert readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Read your proposal aloud to catch awkward sentences and have a non-expert read it for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral reading reveals awkward phrasing; non-expert readers will catch jargon and unclear high-level framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, falsifiable hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Winning proposals present clear, falsifiable hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State testable hypotheses and how experiments/analysis will confirm or refute them; avoid vague goal statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong preliminary data with figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Present strong preliminary data and include figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use figures to convey evidence and feasibility; preliminary results bolster credibility and demonstrate capacity to execute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic timeline with milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a realistic timeline with concrete milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague timelines; tie tasks to measurable milestones and explain contingency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete BI activities with measurable outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define concrete Broader Impacts activities and measurable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify numbers, evaluation metrics, and how outcomes will be measured and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research plan builds on but extends prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan should build on prior work while extending it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate novelty and clear advancement beyond existing work, not merely repetition or incremental tweaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated capacity to execute
rubrics_metrics.description: Show evidence of ability to execute (publications, prior funding, students trained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PI track record, relevant resources, and examples of prior successful projects or trainee outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a dense, prose-only Project Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary that's a paragraph of dense prose loses reviewers' attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make summaries concise, structured, and easy to scan; use clear statements of aims and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid BI boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate BI text undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor BI to the project, provide specifics and evaluation, and avoid copy-pasting generic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague timelines weaken credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific milestones, durations, and responsible personnel; explain how progress will be tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid templated letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support that are obviously templated are detrimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure individualized letters that describe concrete commitments; if a letter is generic, it's better omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention fit into the broader field
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to state how the work fits the broader field is a common loss factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect to field-level questions, gaps, and potential paradigm shifts to show broader significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid aim dependency pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not design an aim or task that requires another aim's success first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims so they are largely independent or include contingency plans; reviewers penalize serial dependencies that risk project failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and style: confident but not arrogant
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a confident, non-arrogant tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be assertive about contributions and feasibility but avoid overstating impact; cite competitors' work fairly and acknowledge limitations upfront.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use figures and white space for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use figures to convey complex concepts quickly and white space to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-designed figures and layout help heterogeneous reviewers grasp key points faster and improve overall impression.
